title: Tenant FinOps Cutover & Governance Playbook
author: Maya Lopez
body:
Summary

This playbook defines the operational and governance steps Customer Success, SRE, and FinOps must follow when performing a tenant-level cutover that changes billing or capacity controls (examples: moving a customer from trial to committed Dedicated, enabling quota-protector webhooks, or toggling per-tenant burst limits). The goal is to ensure cost predictability, tenant safety, and clear rollback paths while minimizing customer-visible disruption.

Scope and When to Use this Playbook

- Applies to any tenant cutover that will alter: billing plan, reserved capacity assignment, per-tenant rate/quotas, or cost-protecting automations.
- Not for routine model version upgrades or small config tweaks that are covered by our standard canary rollout playbooks.

Definitions

- Cutover: The event during which a tenant transitions from one financial/operational state to another (e.g., trial -> paid committed, hosted -> dedicated, or quota cap changes).
- FinOps Gate: A pre-approved financial control threshold that requires Finance + CS sign-off before enabling.
- Safety Net: Automated quota/fallback rules that prevent unbounded spend or dangerous latency regressions.

Stakeholders and Responsibilities

- Customer Success (CS): primary contact for customer comms, scheduling, and acceptance.
- FinOps: validate contract terms, commit levels, and billing triggers; approve FinOps Gates.
- Eng SRE / Platform: implement routing changes, capacity reservations, and alerting.
- Oncall (runtime): 72-hour monitoring and first-responder for incidents.
- Account Executive (AE): commercial ownership, billing follow-up.

Prerequisites (pre-cutover checklist)

1) Contract & Billing
   - Verified signed MSA and SOW in Salesforce with committed throughput and billing start date.
   - Billing metadata (billing_contact_email, billing_entity_id, billing_region) present in tenant metadata.
   - FinOps has generated the pro-forma invoice and validated charge schedule.

2) Technical Readiness
   - Tenant tags: "tier=dedicated|hosted", "finops_commit_id=<id>", and "slo_profile=<profile>" set in tenant record.
   - Capacity reserved: GPU pool assignment and reservation confirmed in capacity inventory.
   - Quotas: quota config (requests/min, tokens/day, embedding-ops/day) created in quota service. Example JSON stored in deployment ticket.

3) Observability and Alerts
   - Dashboards prepared: Tenant Overview, Cost Burn Rate, Token Distribution by Route, Cache Hit Rate, p99 Latency.
   - Alerts provisioned (see Alert matrix section).
   - Billing report configured to deliver daily usage CSV to FinOps and CS (S3 or internal bucket).

4) Communication
   - Cutover schedule agreed with customer and internal teams (UTC timezone).
   - Customer-facing FAQ and rollback expectations drafted.

Cutover Phases

Phase A — Pre-cutover (T-minus 72 to 2 hours)
1. Confirm tickets and approvals: ticket in triage board links to contract and capacity reservation.
2. Run validation script locally or via CI to verify tenant config:

   $ ./tools/validate-tenant-config --tenant-id T-12345 --assert-quotas --assert-tags

   Expected output: PASS for quotas, tags, billing metadata.

3. Snapshot current state: export tenant routing, quota, and billing metadata to the ticket.

4. Create safety net override set: temporary conservative quotas one tier below target for first 24 hours unless FinOps approves full limits.

Phase B — Cutover execution (T0)
1. Put a short maintenance marker on the tenant dashboard (visible to customer): "Planned change in progress — effective <time>".
2. Apply billing plan change via Billing API (example):

   curl -X POST https://billing.internal.redwood/v1/tenants/T-12345/plan
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
     -H "Content-Type: application/json"
     -d '{"plan":"dedicated-committed-v2","commit_units":1000000,"effective_date":"2026-02-01"}'

3. Assign capacity and update routing tags via Platform API:

   curl -X PATCH https://platform.internal.redwood/v1/tenants/T-12345/config
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLATFORM_TOKEN"
     -H "Content-Type: application/json"
     -d '{"tags":{"tier":"dedicated","gpu_pool":"pool-west-3"}}'

4. Apply quota and safety-net policies: post the final quota JSON to Quota Service. Example snippet: 

   {
     "tenant_id": "T-12345",
     "quotas": {
       "requests_per_minute": 1200,
       "tokens_per_day": 2000000,
       "embedding_ops_per_day": 50000
     },
     "safety_net_mode": "soft-guard",
     "soft_guard_thresholds": {"spend_usd":1000, "tokens":500000}
   }

5. Confirm route propagation and capacity allocation in the platform. Watch for immediate alert triggers.

Phase C — Immediate validation (T0 + 0–2 hours)
1. Smoke tests from multiple regions: generation, streaming, embeddings. Use the customer test harness or synthetic runner.
2. Compare baseline metrics (pre-snapshot) to current within tolerance: token rate ±30%, p99 latency <= baseline*1.5, cache hit rate not falling >10%.
3. If safety-net thresholds hit, implement automatic throttle sequence: reduce requests_per_minute by 50% and notify CS & FinOps.

Phase D — Stabilization (T0 + 2–72 hours)
1. 24h: FinOps reconciles daily usage CSV and confirms expected burn rate.
2. 48h: CS calls customer for acceptance check and to confirm no functional regressions.
3. 72h: If metrics stable and FinOps approves, remove safety-net overrides and promote quotas to final values. Otherwise, escalate per rollback decision tree.

Alert Matrix (recommended thresholds)

| Alert name | Trigger | Primary owner | Escalation window |
|-----------|---------:|---------------|-----------------:|
| Tenant: Cost burn spike | spend_rate > projected_rate * 1.4 for 30m | FinOps | 30m -> Pager -> Eng SRE |
| Tenant: P99 latency high | p99 > SLO * 1.5 for 10m | Runtime oncall | 10m -> Pager -> Eng Platform |
| Tenant: Token quota breach | tokens_today > quota * 1.05 | CS/FinOps | 5m -> Auto-throttle -> Pager |
| Tenant: Cache hit drop | cache_hit_rate drop >= 15% | Runtime oncall | 30m -> Investigate |

Rollback Decision Tree (high level)

- If latency or error rate spikes and cannot be mitigated within 20 minutes with route/fallback changes -> rollback to previous routing tag and billing plan.
- If cost spike is due to customer activity but within agreed commit -> engage AE + FinOps to absorb; if outside commit and rapidly increasing -> enable hard-guard quotas and notify customer.

Rollback Procedure (commands)

1. Revert routing tag:

   curl -X PATCH https://platform.internal.redwood/v1/tenants/T-12345/config
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLATFORM_TOKEN"
     -H "Content-Type: application/json"
     -d '{"tags":{"tier":"hosted","gpu_pool":"shared-default"}}'

2. Revert billing plan: call Billing API to set plan back to previous value (store previous in snapshot).

3. Re-apply previous quota JSON from snapshot.

Communication Templates

- Customer notification (pre-cutover):

   Subject: Planned account update on <DATE> — brief downtime unlikely

   Hi <Customer Contact>,

   We will apply your requested plan changes on <DATE> at <TIME UTC>. Services will remain available; we will monitor performance closely for 72 hours and follow up with an acceptance call. If you have a specific traffic window to avoid, please let us know.

- Customer notification (if safety-net throttle applied):

   Subject: Temporary throttle applied to protect account from unexpected spend

   Hi <Customer Contact>,

   We detected a rapid increase in usage and have temporarily limited request throughput to protect against unanticipated charges. This throttle is reversible and will be reviewed immediately by your CS and our FinOps team. Expect an update within 30 minutes.

Post-cutover Tasks and Reconciliation

- FinOps: reconcile daily usage vs projected commit; flag discrepancies >10% for AE follow-up.
- CS: customer acceptance form filled and added to account record.
- SRE: close monitoring dashboard and add any new alerts discovered to the alert library.
- Billing: confirm invoice generation scheduled correctly.

Quarterly Review and Handover

- CS + FinOps will include the tenant in the next QBR if commit >= $50k/mo or if any cutover required manual FinOps interventions. QBR items should include: usage trend, cost-per-1k tokens, cache optimisation opportunities, and recommendations for model/quantization adjustments.

Runbook Annexes

- Example Grafana alert rule (pseudo):

   alert: TenantCostSpike
   expr: increase(tenant_spend_usd_total{tenant_id="T-12345"}[30m]) / (expected_rate) > 1.4
   for: 30m

- Quota API example (JSON) — see "quotas.json" attached to ticket.

Operational Notes and Best Practices

- Always snapshot before any cutover and keep the snapshot in the ticket; it is the single source for rollback.
- Prefer "soft-guard" for first 24–72 hours unless customer explicitly requests full limits at T0.
- Automate daily usage exports to reduce manual reconciliation errors.
- Ensure AE is copied on FinOps anomalies that may affect contract renegotiation.

Appendix: Acceptance Checklist (to be signed by CS & Customer)

1) Billing plan activated and verified in Billing UI (screenshot attached).
2) Quotas applied and smoke tests passing from three regions.
3) Daily usage delivery to FinOps confirmed.
4) Temporary safety-net policy in place for T0+72h.
4) Acceptance call scheduled for T0+48h.

If any item is not complete, mark cutover as paused and follow the pause checklist in the ticket.
